# CLAUDE.md

Guidance for Claude Code working in this repository.

## Project status: GENERATED BY THE `data-to-production` SKILL ON 2026-09-09

Built from `WA_Fn-UseC_-Telco-Customer-Churn.csv` — 7,043 rows, target `Churn`, positive label
`Yes`. Read [REPORT.md](REPORT.md) first: it carries a PASS/FAIL row and
the measured number for each of the seven rungs. Anything not PASS there is the
real state of this project, whatever the rest of these documents say.

## What this project is

The four-rung ladder — describe, predict, recommend, deploy — on one dataset.
`src/app.py` owns the four tabs and holds no business logic beyond layout and
captions. Under it sit four independent modules: `data.py` (Supabase read/write,
pagination, CSV fallback), `model.py` (baseline, training, leakage demo,
scoring), `agent.py` (probability bands to actions, optional Claude opinion) and
`insights.py` (the generic rung-1 facts). The app imports them by path
insertion, so `src/` is not a package.

`ladder.py` is the runner. Eight steps, fixed order, one JSON result each under
`.ladder/`, and `REPORT.md` assembled from those and nothing else.

## Hard rules

- **`ladder.toml` is the only file that should differ between datasets.** If a
  change belongs in `ladder.toml`, it does not belong in Python.
- **Numbers in documents are measured, never estimated.** Every figure in
  `REPORT.md` came from a step that ran. If the model changes, rerun the step.
- **`.streamlit/secrets.toml` never enters git.** Only the Supabase
  *publishable* key (`sb_publishable_…`) belongs in the app.
- **Never demo on client data.** A Streamlit Community Cloud app on the free
  tier is public.
- PostgREST caps a response at 1,000 rows — `fetch_table()` pages with
  `.range()`. `st-supabase-connection` 2.1.3 removed `conn.query(...)`; the
  working surface is `conn.table(...)`.

## Working routine

One task at a time. Read [TODO.md](TODO.md), mark the next item `[~]`, do it,
tick it `[x]` before starting the next, append a dated bullet to
[WorkLog.md](WorkLog.md), commit and push. TODO tracks the plan; WorkLog tracks
reality, including everything that was never planned.

## Setup

```bash
python3 -m venv venv_webina-sep
source venv_webina-sep/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements.txt

python ladder.py all                # rungs 1-4, stopping at every gate
python ladder.py all --auto --local-only   # rungs 1-3 unattended, then the report
streamlit run src/app.py            # the four rungs on http://localhost:8501
```
